name: Potamogeton

project_scope.installer_dependency: P. nodosus and P. pusillus are source-pool comparison concepts, not canonical species in the checked manifest; Approved Taxa Installer handles any later installation.

look_here_first: Underwater, inspect a leaf AXIL for its membranous STIPULE, then distinguish floating from submerged leaves and compare submerged blade width, petiole length and venation. Seek an emergent flower spike and mature fruit before assigning a difficult species.
shared_genus_traits: Rooted freshwater aquatics with flexible submerged stems and alternate leaves; leaf form can change dramatically with water depth.
Membranous axillary stipules and small flowers in pedunculate spikes; small clustered one-seeded fruits develop after flowering.

shared_structure_examples.plain: Thin, sometimes translucent sheath or flap where leaf meets stem; often more informative than overall leaf color.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: submerged node macro with ruler and stipule exposed

shared_structure_examples.plain: Trace lengthwise veins and fine cross-veins; count only with a clear, backlit blade.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: backlit submerged blade both surfaces with scale

shared_structure_examples.plain: A single plant may have different leaf types above and below water.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: whole attached shoot showing both leaf zones

shared_structure_examples.plain: Tiny flowers form a narrow spike on a stalk; fruitlets are important for confirmation.
shared_structure_examples.photo_role: flowering spike and mature fruit macro with scale

species_comparison_matrix.illinoensis: Typically broad submerged blades; floating blades may occur
species_comparison_matrix.nodosus: Broad floating leaves commonly prominent; submerged leaves may be reduced to long petioles
species_comparison_matrix.pusillus: Narrow linear submerged blades; floating blades generally absent
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Photograph connected shoots from water surface to base; leaf plasticity requires multiple nodes.

species_comparison_matrix.illinoensis: Broad, conspicuously veined blade, generally petiolate
species_comparison_matrix.nodosus: Often long, slender submerged petioles with reduced or absent submerged blades
species_comparison_matrix.pusillus: Very narrow linear blades, typically sessile
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Measure mature submerged blades and stalks with ruler; record water conditions.

species_comparison_matrix.illinoensis: Conspicuous stipule; strong parallel and cross venation
species_comparison_matrix.nodosus: Stipule present; floating-leaf petiole and venation useful
species_comparison_matrix.pusillus: Stipule present; narrow leaf vein number and stipule form require close view
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Macro of stipule and backlit leaf; species-level measurements require authoritative key confirmation.

species_comparison_matrix.pusillus: Shorter narrow-leaved plant with small spikes and fruitlets
species_comparison_matrix.how_to_check: Matched spike and mature fruit images; do not decide from leaf width alone.

look_here_first: Check the leaf axil for a stipule, ruling out superficially similar aquatics.
Record submerged and floating leaf forms on one attached shoot.
Compare blade width, petiole length, stipule shape and vein count with scale.
Confirm using spike, mature fruit and a regional key.
overlap_cautions: Submerged leaves may be reduced or absent on P. nodosus; one fragment may mislead.
P. illinoensis leaf width varies with environment; broad leaves alone are not decisive.
P. pusillus belongs to a difficult narrow-leaved complex; final identification requires mature structures and taxonomic review.
Ruppia and other narrow-leaved aquatic genera can resemble narrow pondweeds; check stipules and reproductive morphology.
